title: Beliefs & Foundations
description: General User → Pro. Familiar belief teachings, broader basics and short everyday applications requiring deeper understanding and connections. Covers dependence on Allah, revelation, messengers, the Hereafter, mercy and accountability. All questions are Pro level within the General User audience; specialist theological disputes and reference-number memorization are excluded.
levelMethod: Pro describes the knowledge and understanding required across all question styles. Styles are not difficulty levels. Requires deeper understanding, connecting familiar teachings and distinguishing common misconceptions beyond Mid, without specialist study. This is General User Pro, not the separate Ultra bank. Editorial classification, not calibrated with learner response data.

review.referenceCheck: Linked Quran passages and hadith texts checked during preparation. Questions and explanations are original educational paraphrases, not verbatim translations. Modern scenarios illustrate the cited principles. This is not independent scholarly approval.

selectionHints.unknownResponse: Use I am not sure as a separate UI action, not a fifth option.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes dependence between Allah and His worshippers?

options.text: Worshippers need Allah; He does not need them
Allah needs worshippers to remain powerful
Both depend equally on one another
Only people without wealth need Allah

questions.explanation: The verses affirm people's need for Allah and His freedom from any need for provision from them.

questions.question: What does Allah's name al-Razzaq affirm?

options.text: Every income is morally acceptable
Allah is the Provider
Effort has no place in seeking a living
A successful employer becomes independent of Allah

questions.explanation: The verse identifies Allah as the Provider, possessing enduring power. It does not make every way of earning acceptable.

questions.question: Which pair of teachings appears together in Quran 4:40?

options.text: Only large wrongs matter and small good deeds disappear
Reward is based only on worldly fame
Allah does no injustice and multiplies good deeds
Good deeds make Allah indebted to people

questions.explanation: The verse joins perfect justice with generous reward for good deeds.

questions.question: How do these verses describe a messenger receiving knowledge of the unseen?

options.text: The messenger acquires knowledge independent of Allah
Every person gains the same knowledge through guessing
The messenger becomes equal to Allah in knowledge
Allah discloses what He wills to a chosen messenger

questions.explanation: Revealed knowledge comes from Allah; receiving it does not give a messenger independent, unlimited knowledge.

questions.question: How do the jinn speaking in Surah al-Jinn describe themselves?

options.text: Some are righteous and others are not
All have exactly the same moral character
Every one of them is an angel
None can be described as righteous

questions.explanation: The verse reports differences among the jinn, including differences in righteousness.

questions.question: According to Quran 22:75, how is messengership established?

options.text: Public popularity creates messengership
Allah selects His messengers
People buy it through donations
Study alone turns a teacher into a messenger

questions.explanation: The verse attributes the selection of messengers from angels and humans to Allah.

questions.question: What does Quran 2:253 teach about the ranks of messengers?

options.text: Every messenger has an identical rank in every respect
People determine rank by nationality
Allah favored some messengers above others
A lower rank makes a true messenger false

questions.explanation: The verse affirms distinctions in rank among messengers without denying their messengership.

questions.question: What continuity does Quran 42:13 describe between Muhammad and earlier prophets?

options.text: A command to worship a different god in each age
Rejection of every earlier revelation
A religion based solely on tribal ancestry
A shared command to uphold the faith

questions.explanation: The verse links the revealed way with the commands given to Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Isa.

questions.question: To whom does Quran 34:28 describe Muhammad as bringing good news and warning?

options.text: All humanity
Only his own tribe
Only people who speak Arabic
Only those alive in Makkah at that time

questions.explanation: The verse describes the message as addressed to humanity, not limited to one ethnic or language group.

questions.question: According to Ayat al-Kursi, what is required for intercession before Allah?

options.text: The intercessor's independence from Allah
Allah's permission
A person's ability to pay for a guarantee
An agreement that can overrule Allah

questions.explanation: The verse makes intercession dependent on Allah's permission, not a power exercised against His authority.

questions.question: When answering doubt about reassembling bones, what further ability does the Quran affirm?

options.text: Only intact bodies can be restored
Resurrection requires a surviving photograph
Allah can restore even a person's fingertips
Humans must reconstruct themselves first

questions.explanation: The passage affirms Allah's power to restore the person in detail, including the fingertips.

questions.question: In the passage about death, what does barzakh refer to?

options.text: A new earthly lifetime after every death
A way to postpone all accountability forever
The name of the final scale of deeds
A barrier lasting until resurrection

questions.explanation: The passage denies a return to earthly life to redo one's deeds and mentions a barrier until resurrection.

questions.question: What feature of the record of deeds alarms the wrongdoers in Quran 18:49?

options.text: It leaves out neither small nor large deeds
It records only what became publicly famous
It changes according to a person's social rank
It depends on whether people kept a diary

questions.explanation: The verse describes a comprehensive record and affirms that Allah wrongs no one.

questions.question: Which human faculties does Quran 17:36 connect with accountability?

options.text: Only physical strength
Hearing, sight and the heart or understanding
Only the ability to speak publicly
Only skills used in paid employment

questions.explanation: The verse warns against following what one lacks knowledge of and makes these faculties accountable.

questions.question: What principle opens Quran 2:256 concerning religion?

options.text: Forced words alone establish sincere belief
Belief must follow the strongest social group
There is no compulsion in religion
A person's wealth decides what is true

questions.explanation: The verse rejects compulsion in religion and distinguishes right guidance from error.

questions.question: What does the Prophet teach about entering Paradise in the cited report?

options.text: Good deeds make Allah's mercy unnecessary
The teaching applies to everyone except the Prophet
Worldly success guarantees entry to Paradise
No one's deeds alone make them independent of Allah's mercy

questions.explanation: The report includes the Prophet himself in the need for Allah's mercy, guarding against self-sufficiency and entitlement.

questions.question: Which two truths are placed side by side in these verses?

options.text: Allah's forgiveness and mercy, and the seriousness of His punishment
Mercy for famous people and no accountability for others
Punishment without any possibility of mercy
Forgiveness that makes every action equally right

questions.explanation: The passage gives assurance of Allah's mercy alongside a serious warning, rather than erasing either truth.

questions.question: What should someone who has wronged another person seek before the Last Day?

options.text: A larger audience to defend the wrong
Release from the wrong and the person's pardon
A way to make worldly status replace accountability
Permission to ignore it after doing an unrelated good deed

questions.explanation: The hadith warns that unresolved wrongs can be settled through deeds on the Last Day rather than money.

questions.question: What purpose for creating death and life is stated in Quran 67:2?

options.text: Testing who receives the most public attention
Making earthly comfort the only measure of success
Testing which people are best in deeds
Removing the need for responsible choices

questions.explanation: The verse describes life as a test concerned with the quality of deeds.

questions.question: In Satan's speech after judgment, how does he describe his influence over his followers?

options.text: He had authority that removed all their responsibility
He could save everyone who followed him
His promises were as reliable as Allah's
He called them and they responded

questions.explanation: The verse depicts Satan admitting his failed promises and the followers' own response to his invitation.

questions.question: Why is worship not a service that supplies something Allah lacks?

options.text: Allah is self-sufficient, while people depend on Him
Allah needs only the worship of wealthy people
Worship gives Allah knowledge He previously lacked
Human praise is the source of Allah's power

questions.explanation: The verses distinguish the Creator's self-sufficiency from the creature's dependence. Worship does not meet a deficiency in Allah.

questions.question: How can seeking a living fit belief that Allah is the Provider?

options.text: Work proves provision exists outside Allah's authority
Ordinary effort can be a means through which His provision reaches us
Belief requires refusing every means of earning
Only unexpected gifts can count as provision

questions.explanation: One verse names Allah as Provider; the other calls people to move through the earth and eat from His sustenance.

questions.question: Why does generous reward for good deeds not imply injustice?

options.text: Justice requires denying every generous reward
Reward must depend on other people's losses
Allah can bestow extra favor while wronging no one
Grace means good and evil are treated identically

questions.explanation: The verse itself joins freedom from injustice with multiplied reward. Justice and generosity are not opposites.

questions.question: Why is revelation about an unseen event different from a person's claim to know everything independently?

options.text: Any correct prediction proves unlimited knowledge
A messenger's knowledge must be identical to Allah's
Every hidden matter becomes known to all people after one revelation
Revelation is knowledge Allah grants, not knowledge independent of Him

questions.explanation: The verses locate knowledge and disclosure with Allah. A disclosed matter does not mean unlimited access to every unseen matter.

questions.question: Which assumption conflicts with the jinn's description in Quran 72:11?

options.text: All jinn must have the same moral character
Some jinn are righteous
Jinn are not morally identical to one another
The Quran reports differences among them

questions.explanation: The verse explicitly describes different groups, including righteous jinn and others unlike them.

questions.question: Why does being a knowledgeable teacher not itself establish messengership?

options.text: Every teacher automatically receives prophetic revelation
Messengership is Allah's selection, not a qualification people confer
A large following is the decisive test
The public can vote a person into messengership

questions.explanation: Learning can make someone a teacher; the verse gives the choice of messengers to Allah.

questions.question: How can belief in all messengers fit Allah favoring some above others?

options.text: Believing all means denying every difference in rank
Differences in rank permit rejection of some true messengers
Accepting all as true messengers does not require identical ranks
Only the highest-ranked messenger was sent by Allah

questions.explanation: The verses address different matters: accepting Allah's messengers and recognizing distinctions Allah grants among them.

questions.question: Does a shared revealed faith mean every community received identical detailed laws?

options.text: Yes, every practical law must be identical
No, because the prophets taught unrelated gods
Yes, so no later guidance can ever govern practice
No, shared foundations can coexist with different prescribed laws

questions.explanation: The passages describe continuity in the faith and distinct laws and ways prescribed for communities. These teachings do not contradict one another.

questions.question: Why does the Quran's Arabic language not restrict Muhammad's message to Arabs?

options.text: The stated audience is all humanity
Language automatically limits a message to one ethnicity
Only native speakers can be addressed by revelation
A translation creates an entirely new prophet's message

questions.explanation: The verse explicitly describes the scope of the mission as humanity, rather than one language community.

questions.question: Which understanding of intercession preserves Allah's authority?

options.text: An intercessor can force Allah to change a judgment
An intercessor acts only with Allah's permission
Intercession can be bought independently of Allah
A created being shares Allah's ultimate authority

questions.explanation: The verse rules out intercession exercised independently of Allah's permission.

questions.question: Why does bodily decay not establish that resurrection is beyond Allah's power?

options.text: Human inability to reconstruct a body limits Allah
Resurrection depends on perfect preservation by people
The passage affirms His ability to reassemble and restore the body
Only recognizable remains can be restored by Allah

questions.explanation: The Quran answers doubt about bones with an affirmation of even more detailed restoration. Human limitations are not the measure of Allah's power.

questions.question: What is the problem with planning to return after death to finish neglected duties?

options.text: Everyone is promised another earthly chance
Only popular people may return to complete their plans
Resurrection means repeating the same earthly life indefinitely
The passage rejects a return to redo earthly deeds

questions.explanation: The request to return and do good is refused in the passage, which then mentions the barrier until resurrection.

questions.question: What does the record of deeds imply about wrongs that escape public attention?

options.text: Lack of publicity does not erase accountability
Only public scandals can appear in the record
Deleting a message deletes every responsibility
An action counts only if people can still prove it

questions.explanation: The verse's comprehensive record is not limited to deeds that became famous or remained in human records.

questions.question: How does accountability for hearing, sight and understanding affect claims we repeat?

options.text: Confidence removes the need for knowledge
We should distinguish what we know from what we merely assume
A popular claim becomes certain by repetition
Religious enthusiasm makes accuracy unnecessary

questions.explanation: The verse connects responsible use of our faculties with avoiding claims unsupported by knowledge.

questions.question: Why is pressuring someone to say words of belief different from helping them understand faith?

options.text: Force makes the content of every statement true
Sincerity depends only on the loudness of a declaration
Compulsion is not the same as willing conviction
Understanding is unnecessary whenever pressure succeeds

questions.explanation: The verse rejects compulsion in religion. A forced declaration should not be confused with genuine conviction.

questions.question: Does needing Allah's mercy mean that good deeds are pointless?

options.text: Yes, so all obedience becomes unnecessary
Yes, effort would contradict mercy
No, because enough deeds make Allah dependent on us
No, believers should do good without treating deeds as a claim of entitlement

questions.explanation: The hadith teaches dependence on mercy, while the verse connects faith and righteous deeds with reward. Humility and effort belong together.

questions.question: Which attitude keeps the two teachings in these verses together?

options.text: Hope in mercy while taking wrongdoing seriously
Assurance that deliberate wrongdoing never matters
Certainty that no sinner can be forgiven
Ignoring mercy to make every warning harsher

questions.explanation: The verses support hope without carelessness and warning without denying Allah's mercy.

questions.question: Why do unrelated good deeds not make another person's unresolved rights unimportant?

options.text: A public good deed cancels every private debt automatically
The hadith describes accountability for wrongs against people
Only wrongs involving money can matter
The victim's rights depend on the wrongdoer's popularity

questions.explanation: The report warns that a person's good deeds can be affected by unresolved oppression. Doing good does not justify disregarding someone's rights.

questions.question: Why is counting impressive-looking activities not a complete measure of the test of life?

options.text: Only activities noticed by others have value
Quality and responsibility never matter
The verse concerns who is best in deeds, not outward quantity alone
The person with the longest list must be best

questions.explanation: The verse directs attention to excellence in deeds rather than a competition in visible totals.

questions.question: Why does blaming Satan not settle responsibility for deliberate wrongdoing?

options.text: Satan accepts all consequences on the person's behalf
Every temptation makes the resulting act compulsory
Satan's false promise changes a wrong into a right
Temptation does not erase the person's response and choice

questions.explanation: In the verse, Satan admits calling people while they responded. He cannot rescue them from the consequences.

questions.question: A speaker says Allah would become weaker if people stopped worshipping Him. Which response fits the verses?

options.text: Allah does not depend on people's worship for His power
Only the worship of certain nations sustains His power
His power rises with the number of worshippers
He needs worship only during difficult times

questions.explanation: Allah's self-sufficiency means His power is not supplied by human worship. People remain dependent on Him.

questions.question: Someone refuses reasonable work because Allah is the Provider. Which response best connects the teachings?

options.text: Assume earning always conflicts with reliance
Seek provision through appropriate means while relying on Allah
Treat only money received without effort as provision
Believe successful work removes all dependence on Allah

questions.explanation: Seeking a living is compatible with recognizing Allah as Provider; using means does not make them independent of Him.

questions.question: A learner thinks multiplying a good deed's reward must conflict with justice. What explains the verse?

options.text: Every extra reward requires injustice to someone else
Justice means Allah cannot grant any favor
Allah can be generous without wronging anyone
Only identical outcomes for every person count as justice

questions.explanation: The verse affirms both that Allah does no injustice and that He multiplies good deeds.

questions.question: A classmate says a prophecy means the messenger independently knew every hidden matter. What needs correcting?

options.text: One revealed event makes all unseen matters equally known
Revelation must come from the messenger's own power
Every accurate statement about the future is self-generated
A revealed matter does not establish independent, unlimited knowledge

questions.explanation: The verses distinguish Allah's knowledge from knowledge He discloses to a messenger He chooses.

questions.question: A discussion claims every jinn is necessarily evil. Which correction follows the verse?

options.text: The Quran describes righteous jinn as well as others
Jinn and angels are interchangeable names
All jinn share exactly one moral condition
No jinn can ever be described as righteous

questions.explanation: Surah al-Jinn reports moral differences among them. Their being unseen does not justify ignoring what revelation says.

questions.question: A group says its vote can turn a respected teacher into a messenger of Allah. What principle applies?

options.text: Enough votes create revelation
People cannot confer Allah's selection by voting
Respect from students is itself messengership
Teaching ability automatically carries the same status

questions.explanation: The verse assigns the selection of messengers to Allah, not to a community's decision.

questions.question: A friend says belief in all messengers requires denying that Allah favored some. What is the correct distinction?

options.text: Only equally ranked people can be true messengers
Accepting one messenger requires rejecting the others
All are accepted as true, while Allah grants differences in rank
Differences in rank are decided by our preferences

questions.explanation: Belief in all messengers and Allah's distinctions among them are both taught in the Quran.

questions.question: Someone says different prescribed laws prove the prophets could not share a common faith. Which answer fits the passages?

options.text: Every difference in law means a different Creator
No prophet received guidance for practice
A common faith means every historical rule remains identical
Shared foundations do not require identical detailed laws

questions.explanation: The Quran teaches continuity in the revealed faith alongside differences in prescribed law and way.

questions.question: An app description says Islam's message addresses only people born into an Arab family. What should it say?

options.text: The message addresses humanity, beyond ethnic origin
It addresses only native Arabic speakers
It addresses only people descended from the Prophet's tribe
Ethnic ancestry decides whether its guidance is relevant

questions.explanation: The mission described in the verse is directed to humanity rather than a single ancestry group.

questions.question: Someone sells a promise of intercession that supposedly overrides Allah's decision. Which belief rules out the claim?

options.text: A high payment creates authority above Allah's
Intercession depends on Allah's permission
An intercessor is independent of the Creator
A confident promise removes the need for Allah's permission

questions.explanation: Ayat al-Kursi does not allow an independent power that can compel or overrule Allah.

questions.question: A video claims a body must stay intact for Allah to resurrect it. Which response reflects the passage?

options.text: Human preservation is what makes resurrection possible
Only bodies with every bone present can be raised
Allah's power to restore is not limited by decay
Loss of a body part defeats Allah's power

questions.explanation: The passage answers doubt about reassembling bones by affirming Allah's ability to restore even the fingertips.

questions.question: Someone plans to ignore good deeds now and return after death to do them. What should they reconsider?

options.text: Everyone can request an extra earthly lifetime
Good deeds become possible only after death
The barrier means earthly duties never mattered
The passage gives no such second earthly opportunity

questions.explanation: The request to return and do good is refused. The passage encourages taking the present opportunity seriously.

questions.question: A person thinks deleting the only online record of a deliberate wrong ends all accountability. Which reminder fits the verse?

options.text: Human deletion does not erase Allah's record of deeds
Only actions preserved on a device can be recorded
A missing screenshot makes the wrong become right
People control the final record by editing their files

questions.explanation: The Quran's account of the record is not dependent on human storage. Responsibility requires addressing the wrong, not merely hiding evidence.

questions.question: A religious claim sounds inspiring, but you do not know whether it is true. Which response fits the verse?

options.text: Repeat it as certain because it feels uplifting
Check it before presenting it as established knowledge
Treat confidence as a substitute for evidence
Assume popularity removes responsibility for accuracy

questions.explanation: The verse warns against following what one lacks knowledge of. Religious claims also call for responsible use of what we hear and understand.

questions.question: Someone proposes threats to make a non-Muslim friend declare belief. Which response follows the verse's principle?

options.text: Use threats if the words are religiously correct
Count fear alone as sincere conviction
Explain faith without coercing the person's declaration
Assume pressure removes the need for understanding

questions.explanation: The verse rejects compulsion in religion. Explaining faith differs from forcing a declaration.

questions.question: A regular worshipper says their deeds mean they no longer need Allah's mercy. What should they remember?

options.text: Enough visible worship makes mercy unnecessary
The Prophet alone needed mercy
Needing mercy makes every good deed worthless
Continue doing good while remaining dependent on Allah's mercy

questions.explanation: The hadith includes the Prophet in dependence on Allah's mercy. The verse also affirms the value of faith and righteous deeds.

questions.question: A friend uses Allah's mercy as a reason to dismiss deliberate wrongdoing. What reminder preserves the passage's balance?

options.text: Hope in forgiveness should go with taking Allah's warning seriously
Mercy means deliberate wrongdoing is always harmless
Warnings prove forgiveness is impossible
Only fear matters; hope has no place

questions.explanation: The passage places mercy and warning together. It supports turning toward Allah without treating wrongdoing lightly.

questions.question: You withheld someone's money and want to put things right. What fits the hadith's warning?

options.text: Do an unrelated good deed and keep the money
Settle the person's right and seek pardon appropriately
Wait until public praise makes the matter disappear
Assume religious knowledge cancels what is owed

questions.explanation: The hadith urges resolving wrongs against people before the Last Day. Their rights should not be ignored in the name of other good deeds.

questions.question: A quiz result shows many correct answers. Which response best fits life being a test of deeds?

options.text: Assume the score alone proves acceptance of every deed
Treat knowledge as a substitute for acting responsibly
Use what you know to improve how you live
Use the result to declare yourself better than everyone

questions.explanation: Knowledge can support action, but the verse directs attention to excellence in deeds. A quiz result is not a judgment of a person's standing before Allah.

questions.question: After knowingly making a harmful choice, someone says Satan bears all the blame. What should they understand?

options.text: Satan's invitation automatically cancels accountability
The harm becomes lawful if temptation was strong
Satan guarantees rescue from every consequence
Temptation does not remove their responsibility to correct the wrong

questions.explanation: The verse portrays Satan admitting that he called and people responded. Blaming him does not replace taking responsibility for one's deliberate action.
